name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in dry-run mode on a single low-traffic branch in the main repo for one week. This lets us test real-world impact without risking the main codebase, while still collecting meaningful data on review quality and false positives. The trade-off is slower feedback—dry-run won’t block bad PRs—but it avoids the chaos of enforcing changes on unsuspecting teams. If the results prove valuable, we can escalate to enforce mode on a forked repo next.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower feedback—it’s that dry-run normalizes noise. PR-Agent’s false positives will clutter the branch with comments that get ignored, training the team to dismiss *all* automated feedback. Instead, run it on a *stale* PR (already merged but not deployed) for one week; the trade-off is zero risk to active work, but you’ll still measure review quality against a known baseline. Settle it by comparing the stale PR’s post-merge issues with PR-Agent’s output—if the noise ratio is worse, scrap the idea.
